events.title: Acorn Archimedes released
events.summary: Acorn Computers began shipping the Archimedes in June 1987 — the first home computer powered by the ARM processor Acorn designed in-house.
events.about: The Archimedes ran RISC OS on the ARM1/ARM2 CPU Acorn created when 68000 and x86 chips seemed too power-hungry. ARM went on to power every smartphone and Apple silicon Mac — but it started here in a British school computer. Developers wrote in BBC BASIC and C on a architecture that now ships billions of chips a year.

narrative.whyChosen: The Archimedes was the first commercial product using the ARM architecture.
narrative.whyImportant: ARM processors in every phone and Apple M-series chip trace their lineage to this machine.
narrative.problemSolved: Acorn needed a faster, cooler CPU than off-the-shelf chips for education and home markets.
